title: Reachable services
prompt:
Return how many services a request starting at service start can reach by following one-way call edges [from, to] among services 0 to n - 1, counting start itself.

- 1 <= n <= 100,000 and 0 to 200,000 edges; 0 <= start < n.
- Edges may repeat and may point from a service to itself.
- Return a single integer between 1 and n.
hints: Edges only go one way, so ask which services you can walk to from start, not which ones are connected to it.
Build an adjacency list and run a depth-first or breadth-first search from start.
Mark a service as seen the moment you push it, so each service is counted and expanded exactly once.

solution.explanation: An iterative depth-first search from start visits exactly the services reachable along edge directions. Marking a service as seen when it is pushed guarantees each one is counted once, and the explicit stack avoids recursion-depth limits on long chains.

complexity.notes: m is the number of edges. Every reachable node is expanded once and every edge out of it is scanned once.

followUps: How would you find every service that can reach a given service, rather than the ones it can reach?
